claims.text: Opening the wire under the Dinis lens gives a week of industry news read as the author: forty stories across five beats, twenty-five reaching him through a named concern and fourteen withheld with the reason.
claims.quote: Twenty-five of them reach me through a concern the vault knows I have; fourteen are withheld, each with the reason.

claims.text: The newsroom did not write any of the news, does not store it, and could not change a word of it; the news is in an encrypted vault a different agent keeps.
claims.quote: the newsroom did not write any of it, does not store any of it, and could not change a word of it if it wanted to

claims.text: The vault u9i9jp0l was written by a wire desk agent on 11 October at 16:16 UTC: 40 stories, 55 sources, 7 personas, a join of 280 rows, five design documents and a runbook, in one commit of 24 files.
claims.quote: 40 stories, 55 sources, 7 personas, a join of 280 rows, five design documents and a runbook, in one commit of 24 files

claims.text: newsroom.sgit.ai holds the read key in a config file, published on purpose, and three pages open the vault in the reader's browser, decrypt it with Web Crypto and draw it as text; the write key is with the desk.
claims.quote: The write key is with the desk; the site has never seen it.

claims.text: A commit to the vault is on the page within two minutes: the page re-checks the head pointer every two minutes and caches for good the objects that cannot change, with no release of the site.
claims.quote: The page re-checks the vault's head pointer every two minutes and caches for good the objects that cannot change.

claims.text: The lens is the vault's own join: six public personas and one named reader, and under a lens the page shows what reached that reader, through which concern, and what was withheld and why.
claims.quote: The lens is the vault's own join.

claims.text: Each story has the same shape: headline, date, primary source and kind, confidence, summary, one exact quote with its source, why it matters, who else covered it, entities and personas.
claims.quote: Each story is the same shape.

claims.text: The personal brief under the author's lens is allowed because he is a named reader by his own agreement while the wire is a beta, and like everything in the vault the brief is public.
claims.quote: A named reader, by their own agreement while the wire is a beta. Like everything in the vault, this brief is public.

claims.text: The vault was made in a session the author was not in, by an agent working from a voice brief, and its README says it is a first pass, 11 October 2026, not yet reviewed by a person.
claims.quote: a first pass, 11 October 2026, built by research agents, not yet reviewed by a person

claims.text: 127 publishers were seen and 176 coverage links checked to get to the 40 stories, 8 per beat except 10 for cybersecurity and 6 for governance.
claims.quote: 127 publishers were seen and 176 coverage links checked to get there.

claims.text: Sources carry a tier: A is an open licence and may be kept and shown; B is a primary source not openly licensed, a quote of 25 words or fewer and a link; C is commercial press, headline, link and date, never the text.
claims.quote: Tier C is commercial press and paywalls: headline, link and date, never the text.

claims.text: The join in deliveries.json has 280 rows, one per story and persona, and the rule is a short Python file whose first line says this is code, not a model; entity match counts 3, a desk tag 2, a keyword 2, the right beat 1.
claims.quote: Entity match counts 3, a tag by the research desk 2, a keyword 2, the right beat 1, and each concern counts once at its strongest match.

claims.text: An independent fact check of 10 stories found 3 to correct, and the corrections were made.
claims.quote: An independent check of 10 stories, which found 3 to correct, and the corrections made.

claims.text: The desk is four roles writing only in their own folders: a Poller that never judges importance, a Clusterer that never writes prose, an Extractor that never invents an entity, a Writer that never invents a quote; the Editor places.
claims.quote: The Editor, a person or the newsroom's Editor role, places stories on the front; the desk only proposes.

claims.text: Before a commit a gate fails the run on a quote not found in frozen bytes, a tier-C quote, a missing date or licence line, or a story marked confirmed with fewer than two independent sources; stop conditions end the run instead of publishing.
claims.quote: the gate failing twice, more than 30 per cent of sources degraded, a story about a named private individual

claims.text: What is new is that the desk is a different agent from the one that runs the site, and the only thing between them is the vault.
claims.quote: What is new is that the desk is a different agent from the one that runs the site, and the only thing between them is the vault.

claims.text: The newsroom's agent found the vault on the afternoon of 11 October and released the wire at 23:51 UTC as v0.9.0, with the commit message as the design.
claims.quote: released the wire at 23:51 UTC as v0.9.0

claims.text: The site reads the vault in five steps in the browser, with sgit.ai's vault reader cut down to 182 lines and a drawing file of 214 lines that makes a link only from a value starting with http; nothing from the vault is run.
claims.quote: Nothing from the vault is run.

value.unit: lines of the vendored vault reader

claims.text: The read key is public on purpose: it can read every file and commit and cannot write, so everything in the vault is public for ever, because a published read key cannot be withdrawn from anyone who has fetched the objects.
claims.quote: a published read key cannot be withdrawn from anyone who has fetched the objects

claims.text: The contract between vault and site is written on the how page in words a person can read and a test can check: bundle shape, sixteen named story fields, five delivery fields, status shown as written, and nothing private in the vault.
claims.quote: in words a person can read and a test can check

claims.text: A file of checks runs in Chromium against the real vault in CI: twenty-three checks at v0.9.0, twenty-eight by v0.9.3.
claims.quote: Twenty-three checks at v0.9.0, twenty-eight by v0.9.3.

claims.text: The newsroom's agent cloned the vault and read it in full before it published the read key, and found no key, token or credential in it.
claims.quote: Publishing a read key is publishing everything the key opens, for good, and you do not do that on trust.

claims.text: The agent flagged two things for the vault's keeper rather than fix them itself: a persona and note aimed at one named reader about to become public, and the plan to keep tier-B bytes and feedback, which needs a vault of its own.
claims.quote: it found two things it would not fix itself but flagged for the vault's keeper

claims.text: The named-reader flag was resolved at 00:54 UTC on 12 October in v0.9.3: the author agreed in writing to be the wire's named reader while it is a beta, and the dated record in the config file is what offers the lens.
claims.quote: No other named person gets one without a recorded agreement, and the how page's contract now says so.

claims.text: The three ordinary ways to get one agent's work in front of another's readers, pushing pages, calling an API, or sharing a session, each cost something; a vault is the fourth way.
claims.quote: A vault is the fourth way, and it has properties the others do not.

claims.text: The site owns the presentation and the vault owns the news; neither can do the other's job because neither has the other's key, and updating is a commit, not a release.
claims.quote: Neither can do the other's job, because neither has the other's key.

claims.text: The server sees only ciphertext, sizes, times and random-looking ids; it cannot read a story or tell who reads, so the newsroom adds a daily feed without a server.
claims.quote: It cannot read a story, and it cannot tell who reads.

claims.text: The history is the audit trail: every edition is a commit, the head commit's message is on every page, a correction is a new file and nothing is deleted.
claims.quote: so the history doubles as the audit trail.

claims.text: This is how sgit.ai reads its own documents; the newsroom applied the arrangement to a feed written by someone else, the harder case, so the contract between writer and reader had to be written down.
claims.quote: the harder case, because now the contract between writer and reader has to be written down

claims.text: The vault's README calls itself the first step in carrying out the MyFeeds plan, a good idea the author did not use; the morning read is MyFeeds running with him as the first user.
claims.quote: That is MyFeeds, running, with me as the first user.

claims.text: The next turns are written down: a pitched wire story becomes an article inheriting its frozen sources, the Editor places up to three wire stories on the front, a weekly newsletter is cut from the briefs, and feedback needs its own vault.
claims.quote: The next turns of the loop are already written down.

claims.text: It is a first pass, unreviewed: every story carries ai-generated, unreviewed; 22 of the 40 primary sources were not fetched by the research agent; 10 stories were checked and the other 30 have not been.
claims.quote: 22 of the 40 primary sources were not fetched by the research agent, and the page says so on each.

claims.text: The join is matching, not understanding: entities, tags, keywords and beats with four weights; it will withhold a story the author wanted and reach him with one he would not.
claims.quote: The join is matching, not understanding.

claims.text: The personas are the desk's draft of the author: ten concerns and their terms, written by an agent from what he publishes; the morning read that corrects them has not run yet.
claims.quote: The personas are the desk's draft of me.

claims.text: The vault is on a development server and its read key is public, so everything in it is; the contract keeps that safe and one of its two flags is still open.
claims.quote: The contract is what keeps that safe, and one of its two flags is still open.

claims.text: Nothing here is a product: a beta with one named reader, by agreement, on a site with few readers.
claims.quote: A beta with one named reader, by agreement, on a site with few readers.

claims.text: The facts come from the two records: the newsroom's commits v0.9.0 and v0.9.3 of 11 and 12 October 2026, and the wire's vault cloned read-only with its published key on 12 October; the counts are the vault's own.
claims.quote: The facts are from the two records
